items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: Anson, yeah. See? Your bass horn say, whoop, the mellophones and whatnot, they make the answer.

ctx.x: They went to a lot playing. This was down low. And you could, every man was doing this, you could enjoy it. Man can't do drummers. One of the things. Yeah. Two drummers. When we got there, I said look here. Boy.

How much of the old music came from, I think, we were talking to Dick yesterday afternoon, I was thinking that, you know, entrance of the gladiators, that one, it goes into That's A Plenty. Oh, yeah. Right? Well, it's close. It might have some positives. I wonder how much early jazz came out of martial music, brass band music, I mean music that never was written for the 2-4 beat, that was written for the 1-3 beat. I wonder how much early jazz came out of brass band music. You know, brass band music. At one time,…
Well, what do you mean, about special hymns? Yeah. The things we play come out, or the hymn books in the church which you sing.
